ceiling_directive: Construct sensitivity-one full-class scores satisfying a nuisance-independent weighted-shell bound at r of order max{R_NP, r_G, r_F}, including dense occupancy, and combine this upper bound with explicit same-class private converses.
improvement_directive: Resolve full-fiber-pair-lift by constructing the stated score family uniformly over the complete Hölder fibers, including the dense-occupancy regime, and proving the weighted-shell functional is bounded independently of nuisance entropy. Add same-class lower bounds for r_G and r_F so the resulting statement is a genuine two-sided private minimax frontier.
critique: The note does not prove the full-class private frontier named in the project objective: it proves a private test only for a specially constructed signed two-fiber family under sparse occupancy. The r_F and r_pair calculations are fixed-error achievability calculations for that family, not upper bounds for the Hölder class and not matched minimax rates; no formal same-class private converse is supplied either. The shell-selector proposition is purely conditional on sensitivity-one scores with bounded weighted-shell error, while constructing those scores—the load-bearing step—is exactly the open question. Dense occupancy, arbitrary least-favorable priors, and nuisance-entropy cancellation all remain unresolved, so the present result functions as a technical diagnostic or setup note rather than a usable CATE estimation theorem. The framing discloses these limitations, but faithful writing cannot overcome the absence of a full-class estimator, a two-sided rate theorem, or practical evidence beyond the tailor-made finite experiment.
